newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka offers tax, foreign exchange amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka offers tax, foreign exchange amnesty.

text.p: Sri Lanka will offer a six-month tax and foreign exchange amnesty to those with undeclared funds in or out of the country, the government said on Thursday.
"A six-month period commencing from February 15 will be available to any person who wishes to avail himself of the amnesty," a finance ministry release said.
Private studies have said there is evidence that there are substantial funds kept by Sri Lankans in undeclared overseas bank accounts, but the government has not given an estimate.
"The very fact that the government has given this amnesty shows that they expect a substantial return," said a government official who declined to be identified.
The release said the measure was a chance for those who have evaded taxes or violated exchange control laws, to come clean.
Funds declared under the amnesty would have to be deposited in a special account in the National Savings Bank.
Funds being returned must be converted into local currency and deposited in the account within the stipulated six-month period, the release said.
Withdrawal from the deposits in the first two years would be allowed only for investments in agriculture, industry or infrastructure, it said.
